REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver

Since the vertigo is triggered by specific head movements like rolling over or looking up, this strongly suggests Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). I am performing the Dix-Hallpike test to confirm the presence of nystagmus and identify the affected semicircular canal.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive for right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine position, suggestive of BPPV

speaker: Doctor
text:
The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver with horizontal nystagmus confirms a diagnosis of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), likely involving the horizontal canal. I will proceed with the Epley or Lempert maneuver to reposition the otoconia and relieve your symptoms.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
